Settings

Appearance
Off: only the Light/Dark switch above, changed by hand. System: follows your OS/browser's dark mode setting automatically. Clicking Light/Dark above still works in System mode — it holds as a temporary override until the system value naturally catches up and agrees with it again, then automatic switching resumes from there.
Bars
Status barShow the node count / depth / word count strip at the bottom. Also hideable via right-click on the status bar itself, with an Undo toast — this switch is the reliable way back if that toast is missed, since a hidden status bar has no space left to right-click on
Which individual items appear in the status bar strip, independent of the master Status bar switch above. The "⚠ Back up your data" reminder isn't included here — it only ever appears when your backup is genuinely overdue, so hiding it permanently would defeat the point; if it fires too often, raise the reminder interval in Settings → Data & backup instead.
Drag to reorder the right-hand cluster of the status bar (Saved status, backup indicators, theme, text size, author, and Quick Assist). Hidden items still keep their place in this list so the order is ready for when you turn them back on; the left-hand counters (node count, depth, word count) aren't reorderable — they stay in their fixed sequence.
Tab barShow the row of open-document tabs. Also hideable via right-click on empty tab bar space, with an Undo toast — this switch is the reliable way back if that toast is missed, for the same reason as Status bar above
App barShow the very top row (Hub, Account, Settings, Help, Import/Export). Unlike Status bar and Tab bar above, this switch is not a reliable way back if you hide it and change your mind — Settings itself lives in this row, so once it's hidden you can't get back in here. Use Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A, or right-click the editor canvas for "Show app bar," instead
Hide buttons you don't reach for often, to leave more room for Documents/Templates. Settings and Documents/Templates always stay — Settings needs to stay reachable, and Documents/Templates is core navigation.

Diagrams
Skip review before generatingRight-click a node → Generate diagram normally opens a review screen first — shape, container, and flow direction per node, pre-filled with a best guess — so you can fix anything before it renders. On: generating becomes one click, using that same best guess (or, on a regenerate, whatever you set last time) with no screen in between. To-Dos
AI features for To-DosExtract action items, Break into subtasks, Status summary, and its highlighting live in Settings → AI, alongside every other AI-powered feature in the app — so everything using your API key and budget is visible in one place rather than split across each panel.
Overdue count badgeShow a small count badge on the To-Dos button itself when you have overdue tasks, so you can tell at a glance without opening the panel.
Row actions"Click to expand" keeps rows compact — click a task's own background to open it and reveal priority/due/link/repeat/rewrite/delete, click again to close. "Always visible" keeps all of that in place permanently on every row instead, without needing to click — less compact, but nothing to open first. The drag handle is separate — turn that on from the header's select/reorder toggle instead, only when you actually need to reorder ("Always visible" also keeps it on, alongside everything else).
Collapse sub-tasks by defaultNew sub-task checklists start collapsed instead of expanded, showing just the progress count until you click to open them.
Collapse completed section by defaultThe Completed list starts collapsed to just its header (with count) when you open the To-Dos panel, instead of showing every completed task. Click the header to expand it any time.
Row elementsTurn off any of these to remove them from every task row — useful if you only use a few of them and want a leaner list. Unchecking one only hides it; nothing already set on a task is lost, and it comes back the moment you check it again.
Auto-expire completed tasksAutomatically delete completed tasks after this long. "Never" keeps them until you delete them yourself.
Keep at mostOnce completed tasks exceed this count, the oldest completions are dropped first. "No limit" keeps everything until expiry or manual delete.

Zen mode
Each button sets all 7 options below at once — pick whichever's closest, then fine-tune individual items if needed.
Hide toolbar by defaultAutomatically hide the toolbar when entering zen mode. If you show it again manually while zen, it stays shown until you exit
Hide File ExplorerAutomatically hide the file explorer when entering zen mode. The header's file explorer toggle button still works normally in zen mode and always overrides this — if you show it again manually while zen, it stays shown until you exit
Hide status barHide the bottom status bar entirely while in zen mode. Off by default — zen mode instead trims the status bar down to just Saved status and the auto-rewrite indicator (plus Quick Assist, if it's normally docked in the app bar — see "Hide app bar" below), regardless of your normal status bar item selection, and restores your normal selection on exit
Hide tab barHide the row of open document tabs while in zen mode. Off by default — tabs stay visible so you can switch between open documents without leaving zen mode
Hide app barAlso hide the very top row (Documents/Templates, Settings, Help, Import/Export) while in zen mode — just the tree (and toolbar, if it's on) remains. On by default. If Quick Assist is normally docked in the app bar ("Dock in app bar" in Settings → Quick Assist), zen mode relocates it into the status bar for as long as zen mode is on, instead of peeking the app bar back open every time you invoke it — your actual "Dock in app bar" preference is untouched and Quick Assist returns to the app bar when you exit zen mode
Use browser fullscreenAlso request the browser's native fullscreen (like pressing F11) when entering zen mode — hides the browser's own tabs and address bar too, not just Sakura's UI. On by default. Exiting fullscreen (Esc, F11, or the browser's own control) exits zen mode too, to keep the two in sync

Editor
Typewriter modeKeeps the line you're typing on pinned at a fixed height — the document scrolls under your cursor instead of your cursor drifting toward the bottom of the screen. Also keeps pace with arrow-key navigation. A manual scroll (wheel/trackpad) is left alone until you type or navigate again
Preview
Options that shape exported PDF files.
BrandingShows a small letter-spaced mark on the cover page of PDF exports, and in the bottom-right corner of every page. Reads "SAKURA" by default, or your own text below. Off by default — and off means off everywhere this applies, including the cover page.
Branding textReplaces "SAKURA" in the mark above with your own company or team name. Leave blank to use the default. Only shown when Branding (above) is on.
Layout
Always expand inlineNote, remarks, and Q&A each show as a small dot next to a node when present — click a dot to expand that item as its own line directly underneath the node, right there in the tree, editable in place. Click again to collapse. This setting flips the starting point: every item begins expanded instead of collapsed, useful for a full read-through pass — the dot still folds an individual item back if you don't want it, even with this on. Off by default.
Timestamps on hoverHovering the tree connector or dot at the start of a node — not the text itself — shows when it was created and last modified. Turn off if the popup feels like clutter while you're just moving the cursor around.
Quick Assist
Quick Assist search boxShow the search / Quick Assist box, currently docked in the status bar (Ctrl/Cmd+K opens and focuses it regardless; Quick Assist can also hide it via a command like "hide search bar" — this switch is the reliable way to bring it back)
Data
Backup all dataSaves every document and folder to a single backup file — also includes AI provider keys and the GitHub Gist token (encrypted if Secure Storage below is on, plain text otherwise). Handle this file like you would a password: don't upload it anywhere you wouldn't put a key.
Restore from backupRestores from a backup file — replaces everything currently in the app
Auto-backup to fileWrites a live backup to a file on disk as you work. Chrome/Edge only — Safari and Firefox don't support this yet.
Up to 5 earlier snapshots of Auto-backup to file, at least 15 minutes apart — the live file always overwrites itself, so this is your way back to an earlier point if a bad edit gets backed up before you notice.
Local safety copyA second copy is kept automatically in a separate browser storage area, in case the main storage gets cleared. Not a substitute for Export.
Undo last restoreA snapshot of what was here right before your last Restore, in case that restore turns out to have been the wrong file.
Remind me to back upShows a status-bar warning if it's been longer than this since your last manual Export or auto-backup write — skipped entirely while signed in with sync healthy, since that's already a live off-device backup.
Warn if this session isn't backed upStrict: the browser's own "leave site?" prompt on close attempt, then this dialog if you cancel it — a real last-chance gate, but you'll see the browser's generic popup. Passive: this dialog only, shown next time you switch away from or close the tab — no browser popup, but a direct close with no prior tab-switch gets no warning at all. Off: neither; the status-bar chip above is your only signal. None of this applies while signed in with sync healthy — that already is an off-device backup.
Why this mattersOpening a new version of this file starts with empty storage (browsers isolate it per file). Export before switching files, then Import right after to carry your data over. Auto-backup and the safety copy protect against accidental data loss, but only Export gives you a file outside the browser.
Reset to default settingsRestores appearance and behavior preferences (theme, toolbar, right-click menu, accent color, and the like) to their defaults. Doesn't touch your documents, folders, or AI provider settings.
Secure Storage
Encrypt keys at restEncrypts your AI provider keys and the GitHub Gist token — in this browser's storage and in local backup files — with a passphrase only you know. Off by default; keys are stored as plain text until you set one. There's no recovery if you forget the passphrase.
Not set up — keys are stored as plain text.
Cloud Backup
What this doesPushes the same full backup as "Backup all data" above to a cloud account of your choice, so you can pull it back down from a different browser or computer. Entirely optional — local Backup/Restore always works without connecting either of these.
Backs up to a secret Gist on your GitHub account. Needs a Personal Access Token with the gist scope — create one here. Stored in this browser only, the same way your AI provider keys are.
Not connected.
Auto-sync on editPushes to Gist automatically ~1.2s after edits settle, same timing as Auto-backup to file. If the Gist changed elsewhere since your last Save/Load here (e.g. from another browser), auto-push pauses and flags it below rather than overwriting — resolve with a manual Save or Load.
Backs up to a file Sakura creates in your Google Drive — scoped so the app can only see files it created itself, not the rest of your Drive. Needs a free OAuth Client ID from Google Cloud Console, with added as an authorized JavaScript origin.
Not connected.
Auto-sync on editPushes to Drive automatically ~1.2s after edits settle, same timing as Auto-backup to file and Gist auto-sync. Only active while connected this session — Drive's sign-in token isn't kept across reloads, so this turns itself off (with a one-time notice, not a nag) whenever the session connection is gone, and you'll need to reconnect and re-enable it next time.
Trash
Keep deleted documents forDeleted documents go to Trash, not gone for good. After this long they're purged automatically — pick "Forever" to only ever remove them by emptying Trash yourself.
Empty TrashPermanently deletes every document currently in Trash. This cannot be undone.
Export & copy
Skip folded sectionsOn: OPML export and copying nodes (Ctrl/Cmd+C) leave out anything under a folded node — only what's currently expanded in the outline editor is included. Off: both always include everything. PDF export is unaffected — it always renders the full document.
Include Q&A in exportsPDF prints each question right under the node it's linked to, same as a note; only questions with no linked node fall back to a final section — bold question, regular-weight answer, unanswered rows marked "No answer provided". Off: Q&A stays in the app only, out of the PDF.
Include node Notes & Code in exportsIncludes each node's attached Note and Code block in PDF exports — every note/code card is included in full. Also controls whether OPML's per-node _note attribute is written. Off: excluded from both entirely, including the small "has a note/code" indicator dots — nothing in the PDF hints that a hidden note exists.
Include Remarks in exportsIncludes each node's linked remarks right after that node in PDF exports; unlinked remarks get their own section at the end. Off: remarks stay visible in the app only.
Folded-content notice in Export menuThe reminder that appears in the Export ▾ menu whenever anything is folded ("OPML skips folded sections… Include them" or the reverse) — same info as Skip folded sections above, just surfaced right where you're about to export. Turn off once you know the behavior and don't need the reminder each time; the underlying setting itself is unaffected.
Cover pageAdd a title page (document title, author, word/read-time stats) before the contents page when exporting to PDF. The small wordmark above the title only appears if Settings → Preview → "Branding" is also on.
Use accent color in exportsPDF exports (documents and the To-Dos list) use your current accent color (Settings → Appearance) for titles, checkmarks, and highlights. Off: every export uses the same fixed color instead, regardless of what the app is themed to at export time — useful if you want documents you share with others to look consistent no matter which accent you personally have set.
Debug Log
Enable debug loggingUncaught errors are always recorded in the background, whether this is on or off — so if something seems wrong, turning this on afterward still shows what already happened this session, nothing's lost. This toggle controls the more detailed breadcrumb trail (save, restore, panel, and AI events) and whether the log below is shown. Rolling log, last 500 entries, in memory only. Never includes your actual note/task/document text, only metadata like node IDs, lengths, and which action ran.

Provider

            

              

                AI Mode
                

                  
                  
                

              

              

                

                  Sakura Hosted AI uses Sakura's own AI credentials — no key to find or paste, and no separate account with a provider. Requires signing in; each signed-in account gets a daily request quota. A real escape hatch still exists if you'd rather not sign in or want unlimited usage on your own dime: switch to "Bring your own key" above instead.
                  Disclosure: when you use this mode, the text for that request (a node, selection, or document, depending on the feature) is sent to Sakura's server and forwarded to a third-party AI provider Sakura selects — not stored on Sakura's server either way. See Settings → About → Privacy & data for the full picture.

▾

                

                

                  All seven built-in providers require their own API key — select one from the Provider dropdown above to see where to get it. GitHub Models requires a fine-grained personal access token with models:read scope. This is a fixed list — Sakura doesn't support adding another API endpoint, so a Content-Security-Policy can restrict outbound requests to these known providers rather than staying open to anywhere. Would rather skip finding a key entirely? Switch to "Sakura Hosted AI" above instead — just sign in.

Fallback orderWhen any error occurs on the active provider (quota, rate limit, or other failure), Sakura retries with the next checked provider in order. The active provider is always tried first. Providers without a saved key are skipped. A toast confirms which provider was used.

Separate from the general settings reset — your documents and other app preferences aren't touched either way.

              

            

          

          

            
Rewrite

            

              
Rewrite max response lengthCaps output tokens for the Rewrite feature specifically (editor and Pad). Generate Outline (2048), Restructure Text (4096), and short tasks like Summarise/Tags already use their own larger or smaller caps tuned to what they do, and aren't affected by this. Raise this if rewriting a long selection gets cut off.

              

                Rewrite prompt
                
                

                  
                  
                  
                

              

            

          

          

            
Auto-rewrite on commit

            

              

                
Auto-rewrite on commitRuns Rewrite automatically on nodes as you finish editing them — no manual click. Queued and sent as a single batched request after a short pause or once enough nodes have queued up (both configurable below), not one request per node, to avoid burning through provider rate limits during continuous note-taking. Uses the same Rewrite prompt configured above — there's no separate prompt for auto-rewrite. Requires a usable active provider — an API key configured above for a BYOK provider, or just being signed in for Sakura Hosted AI; if that's not the case right now (no key set, Secure Storage is locked, or hosted is selected and you're signed out), queued nodes wait rather than being discarded and send automatically as soon as the provider becomes usable again. Turns itself off after repeated AI-call failures rather than retrying silently forever — a separate case from simply not having a key yet. Shows a live status in the bottom status bar whenever it's on.

                
              

              

                Auto-rewrite exclusions — text matching any checked category is left alone, since "form a sentence" doesn't apply to it and rewriting it risks corrupting syntax Sakura parses specially. Unchecking a box lets auto-rewrite touch that category too.
                
                
                
                

                  Minimum word count
                  
                

                Nodes shorter than this are treated as labels, not sentences-in-progress, and skipped. Range 0–20; 0 disables the length check entirely.
                

                  Idle pause before sending
                  
                

                Seconds of no further edits before the queued nodes are sent as one batch. Lower sends sooner but in smaller batches; higher lets more nodes accumulate per request. Range 1–300 seconds.
                

                  Nodes queued before sending
                  
                

                If this many nodes queue up before the idle pause elapses, they're sent immediately rather than waiting — keeps a long capture session from growing the batch past what one request can handle well. Range 2–50.
                

                  Show detail in chip
                  
                

                The status bar chip shows "N queued" and a live "sends in Xs" countdown while a batch is pending. Off: just shows that something's queued, no number or ticking countdown.
              

            

          

          

            
To-Dos AI

            

              
Extract action itemsAdds a button in the To-Dos panel header that reads the current document (or your selected nodes, if any are selected) and proposes a batch of tasks from it, added directly with a single Undo. Uses the same provider/key as Rewrite above, and needs AI Capabilities on.

              
Break into subtasksAdds an AI button on each task, next to Rewrite, that proposes 3-6 concrete subtasks and adds them directly, with Undo.

              
Status summaryAdds a button in the To-Dos panel header that writes a short plain-language summary of your open tasks — what's overdue or urgent first, then general progress — shown in a dialog with a Copy button.

              
Highlight key details in summaryBolds task names and colors overdue mentions, due dates, priority, and status words in the Status summary dialog, using the same colors as the To-Dos row chips — so you can scan it instead of reading every sentence. Off shows plain text.

About

            

              
              Sakura
            

            
A knowledge-management workspace for structured documents and everyday personal productivity — To-Dos in the Hub.

            
Single-file, no build step, works offline once loaded, no account required — sign in (Google or email) if you want your documents to follow you across devices, and use optional AI features (rewrite, expand, outline generation, diagram generation, action-item extraction, tagging, and more) with a provider of your choice.

Privacy & data

            
Everything is stored locally in your browser by default — nothing leaves this tab unless you turn on one of the following.

            
AI features send the relevant text (a node, selection, or document, depending on the feature) to an AI provider; Cloud Backup (Gist/Drive) uploads a copy to that service; and signing in (Google or email) syncs your documents and settings to Sakura's own cloud storage so they follow you across devices. Each of these only happens while connected, and only when you actually use that feature.

            
Which AI provider depends on which mode you've picked in Settings → AI → Provider. With your own API key (the seven built-in providers), that text goes directly from your browser to the provider you configured, using your own key and account — Sakura's own server is never involved. With Sakura Hosted AI, that text instead goes to Sakura's own server first, which forwards it to a third-party provider Sakura selects (currently Groq, Cerebras, or Gemini) using Sakura's own credentials, and returns the response — Sakura's server doesn't store that text either way, only a per-day request count against your account's quota.

            
An account holds your documents, templates, and app settings — including the full Hub (To-Dos) — and nothing else. No analytics or tracking anywhere in Sakura, and other users can never access your data.

            
Signing in with Google only shares your name, email, and profile picture — the same info shown in the account menu, not stored anywhere beyond that. Email sign-in needs only the email and password themselves, handled directly by Firebase Authentication — no separate profile data involved. Google Drive backup, if you turn it on separately, only ever gets access to the files it creates itself, never the rest of your Drive.

          

          

            
Support

            
Sakura stays free, with no ads and no locked features — built by one person in their spare time. A tip is appreciated but never expected.

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Enter → new child — works whether you're editing a node or just have one selected
    •   

  • Type → start editing
    •   

  


          
  

Navigation
  

      

  • Click → select
    •   

  • Shift + Click → range
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Click → multi-select
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + A → select all
    •   

  


          
  

Quick Assist
  

      

  • Lives in the header, where a plain search box used to sit. Ctrl/Cmd + K focuses it and opens the results dropdown from anywhere in the app; clicking directly into the box does the same. Type a plain-English instruction and it's carried out immediately: "get me toolbar," "I don't want file explorer," "get rid of pad," "toggle dark mode" — or just type anything else to search documents, notes, tags, settings, and help. Not to be confused with Quick Insert (Ctrl/Cmd + Space) — a much smaller character-insert menu that opens instead whenever you're actively editing text, described below
    • 

  • An empty box shows a "Try things like…" tip with a handful of example phrases — click any of them to run it as a search immediately, same as typing it yourself; nothing executes without a second click on the actual result. One of the examples, "apply editor's choice," is the fastest way to reach the preset covered below without needing to open Settings at all. Turn the tip off in Settings → Bars & Menus → Quick Assist if you'd rather not see it — the box itself works identically either way
    • 

  • To search just one category instead of all eighteen at once, type a category prefix before your query — "notes: budget" only searches Notes, "settings: dark" only searches Settings. Short aliases work too (doc/docs, note/notes, tag/tags, feature/features, and so on). Q&A, Diagrams, and Remarks each have their own prefix too — "qa: rollout" searches only Q&A questions/answers, "diagram: flow" only Diagrams (title + note), "remark: EDI" only Remarks (text + person + context). Don't want to remember the exact word? Click the icon at the left of the box, or press Space while it's completely empty — either shows a picker inline in the dropdown, navigable the same way search results are (↓ / ↑ to move, Enter to pick). Above the categories, the same picker also lists Show, Hide, Toggle, and Run — picking one inserts that bare word instead of a category prefix, which does something different: rather than scoping a search, it browses everything of that kind (see the bare-verb bullet below). Either way, choosing an entry leaves the dropdown open, cursor ready for you to keep typing and narrow further. A category prefix with nothing typed after it (just "notes: " on its own) shows no results rather than browsing the whole category — the box doesn't have a "show me everything in here" mode for categories, only "search within here," so you still need something to search for after a category prefix specifically; the four verb words above are the exception; each of those does browse everything on its own with nothing else typed
    • 

  • Typing just a bare word — "show," "hide," "toggle," or "run," nothing else — lists everything of that kind instead of requiring you to already know a specific setting's name: "show" lists everything currently hidden that could be shown, "hide" lists everything currently shown that could be hidden, "toggle" lists everything either way regardless of its current state, and "run" lists every available Run action ("new document," "duplicate node," "editor's choice preset," "documentation mode preset," and the AI actions covered below). Keep typing after the bare word to narrow the list further by name — "show tool" narrows to just toolbar-related results, the same as typing "show toolbar" would, just built up in two steps instead of one
    • 

  • On a Mac, if the system's own Spotlight is bound to Cmd+Space (its default), it takes priority over the browser and this shortcut won't fire — either change Spotlight's shortcut in macOS System Settings → Keyboard, or remap this one from Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts
    • 

  • Toggles and search are rule-based, not AI — a fixed set of recognized phrases (show/get/enable/turn on… vs. hide/remove/get rid of/turn off…) matched against a fixed list of settings. Nothing is sent anywhere for these, no API key needed, and it never improvises — if it doesn't recognize a phrase, it says so rather than guessing. The AI Run actions below are the one exception: those do call your configured AI provider, the same as clicking their toolbar/right-click equivalent would
    • 

  • Covers the everyday visibility toggles: toolbar (and its group labels), file explorer (and its filter box), zen mode, dark/light mode, auto-rewrite on commit, timestamps on hover, spellcheck, backlinks, word wrap, outline numbering, the Quick Assist search box itself and its icon-only mode, icon-only Import/Export in the app bar, the hover toolbar, delete confirmation, accent-colored branches, expanded toolbar, and the startup tab/blank-session preferences — plus every on/off switch for a whole capability, whether it lives in Settings → Features (To-Dos, AI Capabilities, Tagging, Quick Assist, Quick Insert) or inside that panel's own section (Focus, Backlinks, Hover Toolbar). It does not cover destructive actions (reset, delete, empty trash) or multi-value settings (themes, sliders) — those still live in Settings, on purpose
    • 

  • Tagging is reachable with a slightly longer phrase than you might expect — "tags feature" — rather than its bare name. That's deliberate: that bare word is also what Quick Assist searches for as content, so a short keyword there would rank a toggle above the search hit you were actually looking for. Pad Panel is qualified too ("pad feature") for a different reason — bare "pad" is already claimed by the command that opens or closes the Pad panel for this session, which is a separate thing from turning the whole feature on or off
    • 

  • Below command matches, a separate row type labeled Run covers one-off actions instead of toggles: "new document," "duplicate node," "duplicate," "editor's choice preset" (or "apply editor's choice"), and "documentation mode preset" (or "apply documentation mode") — or type the bare word "run" with nothing else to list all of them at once, the same way a bare "show" or "hide" lists every matching toggle. These don't have an on/off state to show or an existing value to report — they just do the thing once, the same as clicking the equivalent toolbar or Settings button would. Only safe, additive, undoable operations are ever reachable this way; nothing destructive is offered as a Run action, same rule as the toggles above. "Duplicate node" needs a node selected first — if nothing's selected, it still shows up (so you know it exists) but greyed out with "select a node first" instead of a working button, rather than either hiding it or letting a click do nothing unexplained. Undo means different things per action: for "new document" and "duplicate node" it's the regular document Undo; "editor's choice preset" instead restores every setting it touched (toolbar, file explorer, Pad, hover toolbar, accent, text color, right-click menu) back to what they were immediately before, since none of those live on the document undo stack
    • 

  • AI Run actions — also listed under "run," these are the exception to "rule-based, not AI" above: "rewrite document" (the whole open document, same as right-click → Rewrite document), "rewrite this node" / "rewrite selected" (current selection, single or multiple nodes), "expand node" / "expand into subtree" (needs exactly one node selected), "summarise selection" (needs 2 or more nodes selected), "suggest tags" (needs exactly one node selected), "generate outline" (opens the same topic-prompt dialog as its toolbar button), and "restructure text" (opens the same paste-text dialog). Each needs an API key configured in Settings → AI → Provider and disappears entirely if AI Capabilities (Settings → Features) is off — same requirement as the toolbar buttons they reuse. Unlike the rule-based actions above, these take a moment to run and can fail (expired key, provider rate limit) exactly like clicking their toolbar equivalent would — a missing key or a failed call surfaces the same error dialog either way, not a silent no-op. Undo works the regular way once a result lands, since each reuses the exact same function — and therefore the exact same pushUndo() call — as its toolbar/right-click counterpart
    • 

  • Below any command and action matches, the same box also surfaces matching documents, node text, notes, tags, folders, templates, each document's Q&A, Diagrams, and Remarks, plus To-Dos, and settings/help topics. These rows are labeled Go to instead of Show/Hide, since picking one navigates you there rather than changing anything, and each shows a short snippet of where the match sits so you're not guessing what you're about to open
    • 

  • Clicking a "Go to" result does the right thing for its type: a node-text match jumps to that node and highlights the match; a Notes match expands that node's inline note and focuses it; a Tags match jumps to the tagged node; a Q&A or Remarks match opens that document, expands the node it's linked to, and puts the cursor in it (unlinked ones, which have nowhere to be shown, are left out); a Diagrams match opens that specific diagram; a To-Dos match opens the Hub to that entry
    • 

  • Skips Trash by default. Settings → Trash → "Include Trash in search" surfaces matches there too, across every content type above, clearly marked "In Trash"; clicking one reveals it in the Trash section rather than opening it directly, since restoring is a deliberate choice
    • 

  • Rich-text fields (Notes, Q&A, Remarks) are stripped to plain text before matching, so a search never hits raw HTML markup and snippets always show readable text
    • 

  • The file explorer's own filter box only matches document names, not their contents — for anything inside a document, this box is the one that actually looks
    • 

  • Every document has a status chip — No status by default, or Draft, Review, Approved, Rejected — next to the title field. Click it to open a small menu and pick one; it's a menu rather than a cycle-through-in-order control like the diagram status chip, since jumping straight to the one you want beats clicking past the others first. Existing documents start with no status until you set one; it's never assumed. Duplicating a document resets its copy to No status rather than carrying the original's over, same reasoning as why the title gets "(copy)" appended instead of reused verbatim — a fresh copy hasn't itself been through review or approval. Version History restores status alongside everything else for versions saved after this feature shipped; older versions predating it simply leave the current status untouched on restore rather than guessing
    • 

  • Settings → Bars & Menus → Quick Assist controls the search side of this specifically: a switch to turn search results off entirely (command-only), how many results show at once, and which categories (Documents, Notes, Tags, Settings, Help, and so on) are eligible to appear at all
    • 

  • As you type, the list runs in a fixed order top to bottom — matching commands first, then Run actions, then search results — each labeled with what it'll do ("Hide File Explorer," "Show Toolbar," "Run: New document," "Go to: …") and, for toggles, the setting's current state; ↓ / ↑ moves through the combined list (disabled Run rows are skipped, since there's nothing to activate), Enter runs or opens whichever is highlighted, Esc closes and clears the box, or click any of them directly
    • 

  • Every command and Run action shows a toast with an Undo button — nothing is ever silently applied. Just typing a bare toggle name with no verb ("toolbar," "file explorer") flips its current state rather than doing nothing. If a Run action has its own confirmation step and you cancel that step, nothing happens and the toast says so instead of falsely claiming success. "Go to" rows are navigation, not a change to anything, so there's nothing to undo for those
    • 

  • If a phrase matches more than one setting, all of them show up as separate ranked options instead of Quick Assist silently picking one for you
    • 

  


          


Quick Insert


    

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Space while actively editing any text — a node, a Note, a To-Do, anywhere — opens a small character-insert menu. Same shortcut, same menu, everywhere you're editing text; the full Quick Assist is a separate shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd + K) and stays free even mid-edit, so the two are never in competition for the same key
    • 

  • Actions, in order: Insert em dash, Insert en dash, Insert arrow, Insert check mark, Insert cross mark, Insert middle dot, Insert date/time. Which of these appear (and their fixed order) is configured in Settings → Editing → Quick Insert → Menu items
    • 

  • No typeahead — unlike @mentions or the full Quick Assist, this menu doesn't filter as you type. ↓ / ↑ moves through it and wraps at either end, Enter runs the highlighted action, Esc or resuming normal typing dismisses it. There's deliberately nowhere for a typed query to live except the text you're editing, which this avoids touching
    • 

  • Settings → Editing → Quick Insert → Icon-only row switches the menu from a vertical icon+label list to a compact wrapping row of icons — same actions, same order, same keyboard navigation, just a smaller footprint. Hover an icon for its name
    • 

  • Every action splices directly at the cursor and keeps you in edit mode, so you don't lose your place — the fastest way to get these in, and the reason the menu exists
    • 

  • Node-only actions — Note, Tags, Add question, Add remark, Rewrite node, Version history — live in a node's right-click menu instead, not here, since Quick Insert is deliberately the same small menu everywhere rather than growing extra items only inside the outline editor
    • 

  • Version history… (right-click a node → in the "notes" group of the More panel, or promotable to the quick row via Settings → Right-click menu → Menu items) — shows earlier text for just this one node, drawn from the document's regular version history (captured automatically roughly every 10 minutes of active changes — see the Version History entry below) — skips straight past versions where this particular node didn't change, so a document with 20 saved versions might show far fewer than 20 rows here. "Restore text" replaces only this node's text, through the normal undo stack (Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes it like any other edit) — nothing else about the node (note, code, tags) is touched
    • 

  • Settings → Editing → Quick Insert turns the whole thing off — Ctrl/Cmd+Space then does nothing while editing text, rather than falling back to anything else
    • 




          
  

Appearance & Display
  

      

  • Theme & accent — Settings → Appearance: Light/Dark theme, seven accent colours, and an intensity slider. Auto theme sits below it — Off (the Light/Dark switch only, changed by hand), System (follows your OS/browser's dark mode setting live, no polling needed), or Schedule (switches at hours you set, checked once a minute plus whenever the tab regains focus, to catch changes that happened while it was backgrounded or the machine was asleep). Manually clicking Light/Dark in System or Schedule mode holds as a temporary override until the schedule/system value naturally catches up and agrees with it again — e.g. forcing dark during a scheduled light window holds through the next scheduled dark transition and then continues following the schedule normally from there, rather than reverting within the next check. "Accent colour on branches" (Settings → Layout) tints the tree connector lines with the accent too; off by default so branches stay neutral
    • 

  • Chrome background (Settings → Appearance, below Accent) — five presets: Default (follows the Light/Dark theme), Slate, Sand, Ink, and Rose. Recolors the toolbar, file explorer, status bar, app bar, settings, help, and menus; the editor/canvas writing surface is untouched, so your outline keeps reading against its own background regardless of which preset is picked. Independent of both the accent color and the Light/Dark theme — any combination of the three is valid
    • 

  • Status bar items (Settings → Bars & Menus, under the Status bar switch) — which individual pieces show in the bottom strip: node count, max depth, word count, current depth, current node's word count, saved status, backup connection status, the auto-rewrite indicator, theme chip, text size control, and author field, each independently hideable. The master Status bar switch above still controls the whole strip; this is finer-grained, for keeping only what you actually use. The "⚠ Back up your data" reminder chip alone isn't in this list on purpose — it's an actionable alert that only appears when your backup is genuinely overdue, and permanently hiding an alert defeats it; if it fires too often, raise the reminder interval in Settings → Data & backup instead
    • 

  • Status bar item order (Settings → Bars & Menus, right below Status bar items) — drag to reorder the right-hand cluster: saved status, backup connection status, the backup-overdue reminder, the auto-rewrite indicator, theme chip, text size control, author field, and Quick Assist. Hidden items keep their place in this list, so turning one back on doesn't reset where it sits. The left-hand counters (node count, depth, word count) are a separate, fixed-order cluster and aren't part of this — only the right side is reorderable
    • 

  • App bar items (Settings → Bars & Menus, under the App bar switch) — hide Help, Import, and Export individually if you rarely reach for them, to leave more room for Documents/Templates. Settings and Documents/Templates always stay in the app bar — Settings needs to stay reachable (same reasoning as the App bar master switch above), and Documents/Templates is core navigation. Just below that, Icon-only Import/Export collapses Import and Export down to their icons instead of hiding either outright — a middle ground when you still want one-click access but not the label text; hover either icon for its name. Both are separate from, and finer-grained than, "Declutter app bar" (in the app bar's own right-click menu), which hides the title field, file explorer toggle, and Documents/Templates buttons instead — all of these can be combined
    • 

  • Toolbar — Settings → Bars & Menus → Toolbar: "Show toolbar" hides/shows the icon bar (also toggled by the floating button next to the editor or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + X); "Group labels" adds a caption under each icon group; "Word wrap" controls whether long lines wrap in the editor or scroll horizontally instead; "Expanded" shows the Extras group as buttons instead of a menu. "Sections" lets you hide whole icon groups (History, Structure, Move, Format, Fold, Insert, AI, Extras, Delete) for a leaner bar, and "Insert buttons" trims individual buttons within Insert without hiding the whole group
    • 

  • Editor's choice preset — Settings → Presets → Apply, or Quick Assist as a Run action ("editor's choice" — see below, also one of the clickable example phrases when Quick Assist opens empty): one click reconfigures the toolbar, file explorer, hover toolbar, status bar, app bar, Quick Assist location, editor backgrounds, Quick Insert, layout, and export branding to a curated set for writing and sharing polished output. Toolbar and file explorer start hidden; hover toolbar is turned off; the status bar keeps only Words, Depth, Saved status, and the auto-rewrite indicator, hiding node count, max depth, node word count, the backup-connection chip, the theme chip, the text-size control, and the author field (the Secure Storage lock chip is left alone regardless of this preset, since it only shows itself while actually locked and isn't density-related clutter to begin with); the app bar stays visible with Quick Assist docked in it. Your accent color and node text color are left untouched — this preset is about density and visibility, not color. Note and Code both switch "Match editor background" off, so each reads as visually distinct chrome rather than blending into the outline canvas. The toolbar's own button set is curated for whenever you bring it back (Highlight, Text color, Collapse, Expand, Date/time, Note, Tags, Rewrite, and Delete); the right-click quick row gets Focus, Rewrite, Note, Date/time, Tags, and Delete — Focus lands there specifically because this preset turns off the hover toolbar, its usual home. Quick Insert (the Ctrl/Cmd+Space character-insert menu) switches to its icon-only row with every character action enabled. Export branding turns on with a custom company/team name, and note/remark/Q&A/diagram cards are set to expand automatically. Everything not mentioned is hidden; you can still adjust any of this individually afterward in Settings, wherever that particular control normally lives. However you apply it, an Undo appears — Quick Assist's own toast gets one immediately, and Settings shows a persistent Undo button next to Apply that survives a page reload, so closing the toast or navigating away doesn't cost you the ability to revert. That undo restores every one of the settings above to what they were immediately before, in one step. Applying the preset again (from either entry point) replaces whatever undo point existed with a fresh one taken at that moment — it's a single-level undo, not a history
    • 

  • Documentation mode preset — Settings → Presets → Apply (second card, below Editor's choice), or Quick Assist as a Run action ("documentation mode"): the opposite instinct from Editor's choice, built for long-form structured documentation. Toolbar, file explorer, and status bar are all fully visible with nothing trimmed; hover toolbar is on; Quick Insert shows full labels with every action available. Tagging and Backlinks are both switched on. Note switches "Match editor background" on, so it blends into the outline canvas. Export branding is explicitly turned off — this preset is about writing, not preparing polished output to share. Has its own separate Undo, independent of Editor's choice's — applying one doesn't clear the other's undo point
    • 

  • The tree always renders in a clean indented view, closer to Dynalist or Workflowy — no │├└─ connector characters. Every row gets a small dot instead of a triangle fold-arrow — a folded parent shows as a ring with a dot inside, hovering either kind reveals −/+ — plus a faint vertical guide line per indent level so nesting stays easy to trace. This isn't a setting; it's the app's only tree style
    • 

  • Section markings — Settings → Layout → "Section markings": toggles the coloured accent bar on section-header rows. On by default
    • 

  • Row selection style — Settings → Layout → "Row selection style" controls how selected rows are marked: Fill (default) shades the row background, with the primary/anchor row a shade darker than the rest of a multi-select; Outline traces a thin border, with the anchor row's border and a light fill slightly stronger; Left bar shows an accent-coloured bar on the left edge, thicker on the anchor row; Dot marks each selected row with a small dot, larger and solid on the anchor row. Fill and Outline are neutral/near-neutral; Left bar and Dot use the active accent colour
    • 

  • Layout — Settings → Layout: "Text size" is a slider from 85% to 140%; "Limit reading width" caps line length and centers the tree instead of spanning the full window, off by default (Preview has always had its own separate version of this, always on); "Branch spacing" sets the horizontal indent per depth level (2-6)
    • 

  • File Explorer — Settings → Bars & Menus → File Explorer: control whether new folders start collapsed, and whether a title-filter box appears above the documents list
    • 

  • All of the above are saved automatically and restored next time you open the app. "Reset to default settings" (Settings → Data) reverts appearance and behaviour preferences to their defaults without touching your documents
    • 

  


          
  

Structure
  

      

  • Right-click a node → a small row of four marker icons (Confirmed, Issue, Parked, Follow-up — see the Markers entry below) sits above everything else, always visible and not part of the customizable menu; below that, a row of icon buttons for the most common actions, defaults are Zoom in, Note, Tags, Rewrite, Delete. Click More for move, sort, rewrite document, and everything else. Customise which buttons appear via Settings → Right-click menu — you can also reset to defaults there. Zoom in is also in the toolbar Fold group and via Ctrl/Cmd + .; zoom out via Ctrl/Cmd + , or clicking the same toolbar button again
    • 

  • Markers — five quick marks (✓ Confirmed, ⚠ Issue, ⏸ Parked, 🚩 Follow-up, ✗ N/A) for tracking status on a node, e.g. while reviewing a document. N/A covers something discarded or out of scope — deliberately a different icon from Issue, so "this needs attention" and "this doesn't apply/was decided against" don't collide on the same cross mark. Set from the editor's own right-click menu. Once set, a small colored glyph shows on that node in the editor and in PDF exports. In the editor, clicking the glyph filters the tree to that marker — showing every matching node, its full subtree, and its ancestors back to the root (dimmed, so they read as "here's where it lives" rather than more matches); a filter bar appears with a × to clear it. Right-click the glyph to clear the marker itself instead. A marker filter and a tag filter can both be active together — matching nodes must satisfy both (tag matching itself stays a plain per-node check, unlike the marker filter's subtree behavior).
    • 

  • Right-clicking empty space — editor canvas, file explorer, status bar, tab bar, or app bar — opens a separate, smaller menu of chrome-level actions, not the node menu above. Navigate it with ↓ / ↑ and Enter, same as the category picker above, or hover with a mouse — both move the same highlight. Editor canvas: switch theme, hide/show toolbar, and Collapse all/Expand all sit in the menu itself; a "More…" item opens a second menu at the same spot for the rest — hide/show file explorer, Pad, status bar, or tab bar, "Show app bar" (only appears while zen mode has it hidden), and Settings. File Explorer: switch theme, hide file explorer, Settings. Status bar: switch theme, hide status bar, Settings. Tab bar: switch theme, new document, close current tab, hide tab bar, Settings. App bar: switch theme, hide/show file explorer or toolbar, and "Declutter app bar" — which hides the title field, file explorer toggle, and the Documents/Templates buttons, but deliberately never hides Settings — hiding it would remove your only way back in. (Quick Assist used to share this exemption when it lived in the app bar too; it's since moved to the status bar, so it isn't part of this menu's options at all anymore.) Every hide action here shows an Undo toast, same pattern as Quick Assist's own toggles. If you hide Status bar or Tab bar from their own right-click menu, that specific spot disappears with it — but the editor canvas's own right-click menu keeps the same Status bar/Tab bar toggles, so it works as a fallback, in addition to the plain switches under Settings → Bars & Menus. Declutter app bar has no separate switch by design, since Settings (reachable via the button it deliberately never hides) already reverses it in one click
    • 

  • Backlinks — while editing a node, type @ to mention another node by name; a dropdown filters as you type, pick with mouse or arrow keys + Enter. The reference renders as a clickable link that jumps to the target. Deleting a referenced node removes its links from all other nodes automatically
    • 

  • Tags — select a node and click the tag icon (toolbar Insert group) or right-click → Tags to open the tag popover. Existing document tags appear as chips to toggle; type a new name and press Enter to add. Tags render as #chips on the node. Click a chip in the tree to filter to that tag; click again or × to clear. Multi-select: toolbar button applies to all selected nodes
    • 

  • Checkboxes — click the  toolbar button (Insert group) to toggle a node as a checkbox. Or type [ ] / [x] at the start of a node while editing — it auto-converts on commit. Click the box to check/uncheck. Parent checkbox nodes with checkbox children show a 2/5 progress badge; checking all children auto-checks the parent. Checked nodes are struck through and dimmed. Multi-select supported
    • 

  • Heading shortcut — type # through ###### (1 to 6 of them) followed by a space at the very start of a node, then finish editing — same auto-convert-on-commit as checkboxes above, and sets the node's real heading level (the same field the Heading toolbar button sets), stripping the markdown prefix. Caps at H6, matching the toolbar's own options — #Text with no space, or seven or more #, doesn't convert
    • 

  • ⤴ → insert above
    • 

  • ＋ → add child
    • 

  • Tab / Shift + Tab → indent / outdent
    • 

  • ⧉ → duplicate node / subtree
    • 

  • Alt + ↑ / ↓ → move
    • 

  • Drag a row → drop above/below to reorder, or onto the middle of another row to nest as its child. Dragging any node that's part of a multi-selection moves the whole selection together
    • 

  • Right-click a node with children → More → Sort children (A → Z, Z → A, or by depth — shallowest subtree first)
    • 

  •  Extras in the toolbar → sort all top-level nodes the same three ways
    •   

  


                    


Tagging


    

  • Select a node and click the tag icon (toolbar Insert group) or right-click → Tags to open the tag popover. Existing document tags appear as chips to toggle; type a new name and press Enter to add. Remove a tag from a node by toggling its chip off in the popover
    • 

  • Tags render as #chips directly on the node row. Click a chip in the tree to filter the entire tree to that tag; click the chip again or the × to clear the filter
    • 

  • Multi-select: select several nodes, then click the tag icon — the popover applies to all selected nodes at once. Tags already on all selected nodes appear toggled on; tags on only some appear in an indeterminate state
    • 

  • AI Suggest tags (AI toolbar group) reads the node text and the document's existing tags, then applies relevant ones directly — prefers reusing tags already in the document before inventing new ones
    • 




          


@ Mentions & Backlinks


    

  • While editing a node, type @ to mention another node by name; a dropdown filters as you type — pick with mouse or arrow keys + Enter. The reference is saved as [[Node name]] and renders as a clickable link that jumps to the target node
    • 

  • Deleting a referenced node automatically removes its [[mention]] links from all other nodes
    • 

  • Turning the feature off (Settings → Panels → Backlinks) suppresses the @ dropdown. Existing [[mentions]] in node text still render as clickable links regardless — they navigate on click even when the feature is off
    • 




          


Focus (zoom into a branch)


    

  • Right-click a node → Zoom in (or Ctrl/Cmd + ., or the zoom icon in the toolbar Fold group) → only that node and its descendants are shown. A breadcrumb bar appears above the editor showing the path back to the root; click any crumb to zoom out to that level
    • 

  • Exit focus with Ctrl/Cmd + ,, by clicking the same toolbar button again, or by clicking the root crumb in the breadcrumb bar
    • 

  • Focus state is saved with the document, the same way fold state is — closing and reopening it (even in a new session) returns to whatever branch was last focused
    • 

  • Turning the feature off (Settings → Editing → Focus) hides the zoom-in toolbar button and right-click action, and exits any active focus session immediately. Ctrl/Cmd + . also stops working while the feature is off
    • 




          


Node hover toolbar


    

  • Hover any node to reveal two small buttons — Menu and Zoom in — right next to that row's own bullet, at any depth, including top-level nodes. They fade in only while you're hovering, and don't require selecting the node first
    • 

  • Zoom in acts immediately, same as right-click → Zoom in on branch (or Ctrl/Cmd + .) — see the Focus section above
    • 

  • Menu opens a vertical list of actions with icons and labels — Add child, Insert above, Insert below by default. Pick one to act on the node you were hovering; the list closes automatically afterward. Close it without choosing anything via Esc, clicking elsewhere, or moving to a different node
    • 

  • Settings → Editing → "Node hover toolbar" turns the whole thing on or off, right at the top of that section — "Menu items" below it is a checklist of everything the Menu dropdown can show — structural actions, AI actions, Note/Code/Tags, and Delete. Zoom in isn't in that list since it already has its own dedicated button
    • 

  • The fold/unfold arrow (▾/▸) on any node with children turns into −/+ while you hover it, and clicking it works exactly the same either way
    • 

  • Hovering the tree connector or the leaf dot at the start of a node — not the label text — shows a themed tooltip with when it was created and last modified. It's a separate control from the hover toolbar above; turn it off independently via Settings → Layout → "Timestamps on hover"
    • 





  

Formatting
  

      

  • Ctrl/Cmd + B → bold
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + I → italic
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + U → underline
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + S → strike
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + H → highlight (caret next to it picks a color)
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + F → text color (caret next to it picks a color)
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + 1–6 → apply Heading 1–6 to the selected node(s), independent of tree depth — pick from the dropdown next to Text color, or Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + 0 / re-clicking the same level to return to body text. Combines with bold/italic/underline/strike on top if you want further emphasis
    •   

  


          


Semantics


    

  • **Text** → bold — or select text and press Ctrl/Cmd+B to bold just that selection
    • 

  • __Text__ → italic — or select text and press Ctrl/Cmd+I to italicize just that selection
    • 

  • @Node name → Node name — backlink to another node; type @ while editing to pick from a list
    • 

  • [ ] task or [x] task → auto-converts to a checkbox node on commit
    • 

  • Tag icon in toolbar or right-click → Tags → tag popover (toggle existing tags or add new ones)
    • 




          


AI Rewrite


    

  •  button in the toolbar → rewrites the selected node; with multiple nodes selected, rewrites all of them in one batch; with text highlighted inside an editing node, rewrites just that selection
    • 

  • Right-click a node → Rewrite node is in the quick icon row (Rewrite selection, if multiple are selected); click More → Rewrite document to rewrite every node in the tree
    • 

  •  button next to Rewrite, or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + O → Generate outline (AI): describe a topic and it inserts an AI-generated nested outline into the current document — into a blank doc, or after the current selection; also available as "Generate with AI" on the blank-document screen. Uses the same provider/model/key as Rewrite (Settings → AI → Provider), but its own fixed instructions, not the customizable rewrite prompt
    • 

  • Restructure text (AI) — Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R: paste messy or unstructured text (notes, an email, a transcript) and it organizes it into a tree, cleaning up wording as needed (fixing broken line wraps, tightening long sentences) so it reads well as outline nodes — it will not invent facts that are not in your text, but it is not a verbatim copy either. If the pasted text already has clear structure (bullets, consistent indentation, or literal tree-connector characters), it is parsed directly with no AI call at all. Unlike Generate outline, this always opens as a new document rather than inserting into the one you have open, so an import can never accidentally merge into unrelated work
    • 

  •  button next to Outline → Suggest icon: picks a fitting emoji for the selected node's label and adds it as a prefix (e.g. "🛒 Webshop"). With multiple nodes selected, applies one straight away to each, picked from a keyword list first and an exact match against icons already used elsewhere in your documents, falling to AI only when neither matches. For a single node, if more than one good option turns up, a small popover appears above it to pick from; right-click → More → Suggest icons for all nodes runs it over the whole tree (asks to confirm first). Since the icon is just leading text, removing or changing it is normal editing — click the node and edit it like any other text
    • 

  • Batches larger than 30 nodes are sent in sequential chunks automatically, with a status toast showing progress (e.g. "Rewriting nodes 1–30…")
    • 

  • Expand node (AI) — select a single node and click the expand button in the AI toolbar group to break it into child nodes. Useful for dense labels like "Distribution model (OPML, localStorage, multi-tab sync)" → a proper subtree. AI generates 3–8 children; result is undoable
    • 

  • Suggest tags (AI) — select a node and click the tag-suggest button; AI reads the node text and the document's existing tags, then applies relevant ones directly. Prefers reusing tags already in the document before inventing new ones
    • 

  • Summarise selection into parent (AI) — select 2 or more nodes (Shift-click or Ctrl/Cmd-click), then click the summarise button; AI writes a concise parent label and inserts it above the selection, with the selected nodes indented underneath. The bottom-up outlining pattern — build the detail first, name the group after
    • 

  • Sakura Hosted AI — Settings → AI → the "AI Mode" switch at the top → "Sakura Hosted AI", then sign in. No key to find or paste; Sakura's own credentials handle the request via a small Cloudflare Worker, capped by a daily per-account quota. The request text for that one call goes to Sakura's server and on to a third-party provider Sakura selects, not stored either way — see Settings → About → Privacy & data for the full picture. Selecting it collapses the panel down to just sign-in status — no model or key fields, since there's nothing to configure. Prefer your own key, or want usage with no daily cap? Flip the same switch to "Bring your own key" instead
    • 

  • Settings → AI → AI Mode → "Bring your own key" reveals the Provider dropdown, Model, and API Key fields (hidden entirely under Sakura Hosted AI) — choose a provider, paste the API key for it, then head to the Rewrite section to optionally customise the rewrite prompt. All AI features — Rewrite, Expand, Tag suggestion, Summarise, Generate outline, Suggest icon — share whichever AI Mode and provider/key is currently active. "Reset to default" next to the prompt box restores the original grammar-and-spelling-only wording; "Rephrase" swaps in a different canned prompt that's allowed to restructure sentences and vary wording, not just correct errors — both replace the box's contents and save immediately, the same way, so review before relying on either. There's only one active prompt: switching to Rephrase also changes what Auto-rewrite on commit does, if it's on, since auto-rewrite always uses whichever prompt is currently active. "Reset AI settings", at the bottom of the "Bring your own key" section, restores your provider and model choices, clears every saved key, and also resets the shared rewrite prompt — want just the prompt reset, without touching your keys? Use "Reset to default" next to the prompt box instead. Switching AI Mode back and forth remembers whichever BYOK provider you were last on for the rest of the session (not saved across a reload if you leave on Sakura Hosted AI)
    • 

  • Auto-rewrite on commit (Settings → AI → Auto-rewrite on commit, off by default) — runs Rewrite automatically on a node as soon as you finish editing it, no manual click needed. Only text typed by hand counts: if any part of an edit session came from a paste or drop (checked via the browser's own paste/drop signal on that edit), that node is skipped for auto-rewrite on that commit — paste it, then use the manual Rewrite button if you want AI on it. Committing a node with no actual text change (e.g. clicking in and back out without editing) is also skipped — it doesn't re-queue nodes that haven't changed. It doesn't send one request per node: committed nodes are queued and sent as a single batched request once either an idle pause passes or enough nodes have queued up, whichever comes first — both the pause length (1-300s, default 120s) and the queue size (2-50, default 5) are configurable in Settings, not fixed — built this way specifically to avoid exhausting provider rate limits during continuous note-taking. A small ✦ dot appears next to any node currently queued (or mid-batch, waiting on the response) — click that dot to pull just that node back out of the queue before it's sent — separate from the status bar chip, which shows the overall off / idle / queued-count-with-a-live-countdown / paused / rewriting state and doubles as the control itself: click it to turn auto-rewrite on or off directly (see below for what clicking does instead while it's paused), right-click it for its settings (exclusions, minimum word count, idle pause, queue size). The countdown ticks down to the batch's send time and resets to the full idle-pause value every time another node joins the queue — a fresh edit means a fresh wait, not a shorter one. Both the queued count and the countdown are independently hideable from the chip (Settings → AI → Auto-rewrite on commit, below the queue-size setting) if either feels like more detail than you want at a glance — the chip still distinguishes "something's queued" from idle even with both turned off, just without the numbers; the tooltip on hover always shows the full detail regardless of what the chip itself displays. Exclusions (checkboxes, headings, [[backlinks]]/`code` syntax) and the minimum word count are each independently configurable checkboxes in Settings, not fixed. Needs a usable active provider to do anything — for a BYOK provider that means a key configured above; for Sakura Hosted AI, being signed in. If that's not the case right now — no key set, Secure Storage is locked so the saved one can't be read, or hosted is selected and you're signed out — the chip turns red and shows "paused," queued nodes are held rather than discarded, and the batch sends automatically the moment the provider becomes usable again (e.g. right after unlocking, or right after signing in) rather than waiting for the next edit to retrigger it. Clicking the chip while paused acts as the fix — unlocks Secure Storage directly if that's the cause, or jumps to the key field in Settings if not. That's separate from the retry-exhaustion case: if it fails three times in a row with a key that is available (e.g. an expired key), it turns itself off and tells you why, rather than silently retrying forever. Switching documents discards anything still queued rather than rewriting into the wrong document. Nodes created by Restructure text, Generate outline, paste-a-tree, and Word/OPML import are never queued for auto-rewrite regardless of this setting — only nodes you type into interactively go through commitEdit at all
    • 

  • Built-in providers — seven BYOK providers ship with Sakura: Gemini (free), Groq (free, fast), Claude API, ChatGPT (OpenAI), OpenRouter (free models), Cerebras, and GitHub Models (free, needs your GitHub account). Cerebras's own free access varies by account and model — check their Billing tab if a request fails with a payment-required error. This is the complete, fixed list — Sakura doesn't support adding another provider. All need an API key — selecting a provider shows a direct link to where you get one. GitHub Models requires a GitHub personal access token with models:read scope; model IDs in the dropdown already include the required vendor prefix (e.g. openai/gpt-4o). These seven only show up under AI Mode → "Bring your own key" — Sakura Hosted AI needs no key at all and is the other AI Mode option, see the bullet above
    • 

  • Provider fallback — Settings → AI → Provider → Fallback order: enable the toggle to let Sakura automatically retry with the next checked provider when the active one fails — quota, rate limit, wrong model ID, or any other error. The active provider is always tried first; the list sets the retry order. Providers without a saved key are skipped automatically, and if none of the checked providers besides the active one have a key, a notice under the list says so directly rather than letting it fail silently the first time it's actually needed. A toast names both the failed provider and the one that succeeded (e.g. “Quota hit on Groq — rewritten with Gemini ✦” or “Error on Groq — rewritten with Gemini ✦”). The only error that does not trigger fallback is a bad API key (401) — that surfaces directly so you know to update it. Default order on a fresh install: Groq → Gemini → Cerebras → OpenRouter, with the first three enabled
    • 

  • To-Dos AI — Settings → AI → To-Dos AI, three independent toggles (each on by default): Extract action items adds a button in the To-Dos panel header that reads the current document — or your selected nodes, if any are selected — and proposes a batch of tasks from it, added directly with one Undo for the whole batch. Break into subtasks adds a small AI button on each open task (next to Rewrite) that proposes 3-6 concrete steps and adds them as real subtasks, also with Undo; it's hidden on tasks that already have subtasks or are set to repeat, since those can't hold subtasks. Status summary adds a header button that writes a short plain-language readout of your open tasks — what's overdue or high-priority first, then general progress — shown in a dialog with a Copy button. All three use the same provider/key/model as Rewrite above and need AI Capabilities on (Settings → Features); turning a toggle off here removes just that one button, leaving Rewrite and the other two untouched
    • 

  • Usage today — below the API key field, Sakura counts requests made to the currently selected provider today (and shows the count next to each provider in the Fallback order list once any requests are made). This is a local, best-effort counter — it resets on your computer's local calendar day, which can drift slightly from a provider's own reset clock (e.g. Gemini resets at midnight Pacific), and it isn't fetched from the provider itself. Treat it as a rough gauge of how much you've used a provider today, not an authoritative quota reading — check the provider's own dashboard (e.g. Google AI Studio) for the real number if it matters
    • 

  • Test key — the Test button next to Save sends a minimal request (asks the model to reply "OK") to confirm the currently typed or saved key actually works, without waiting for your next real Rewrite to find out. A toast reports success or the specific error. This check does not count toward the Usage today total above, since it's a connectivity check rather than real feature use
    • 




          
  

Utilities
  

      

  • Ctrl/Cmd + S → save now (kept in-app — doesn't trigger the browser's "Save Page As")
    • 
  

  • Export ▾ has two items: PDF and OPML. PDF always renders the full document, whatever is folded in the outline editor; OPML follows Settings → Export & copy → "Skip folded sections", which also applies to copying nodes with Ctrl/Cmd+C
    • 

  • Import ▾ (next to Export ▾) → OPML imports an .opml outline file as a new document
    • 

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + D / Insert Date/Time in toolbar → timestamp
    •   

  • Copy Tree as Image → PNG
    •   

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + C → copy selection
    •   

  • Clear → reset
    •   

  • Shortcuts that double as OS/browser bindings can occasionally be intercepted before they reach the page — if one doesn't fire, the matching button or menu item always works
    •   

  


          


Maximize / Zen mode


    

  • ⤢ floating button bottom-right of the editor, Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E to toggle it on or off, or Esc to exit only → by default hides the file explorer and app bar, so only the tree, toolbar (if it's on), tab bar, and a trimmed status bar remain
    • 

  • Settings → Zen mode → "Hide File Explorer" — on by default, so the file explorer auto-collapses when you enter zen mode. The header's own sidebar-toggle button (▤) keeps working normally throughout zen mode regardless of this setting, so you can always open or close it manually for that session — same "manual choice sticks until you exit" behavior as the toolbar and Pad below
    • 

  • Settings → Zen mode → "Hide status bar" controls whether the bottom status bar is hidden outright on entry — off by default. Left on, zen mode instead trims it down to just Words, Depth, Saved status, and the auto-rewrite indicator (plus Quick Assist, if it's normally docked in the app bar — see below), regardless of your normal status bar item selection, and restores your normal selection when you exit
    • 

  • Settings → Zen mode → "Hide tab bar" controls whether the row of open document tabs is hidden on entry — off by default, so you can switch between open documents without leaving zen mode. Turn it on if you'd rather it disappear too
    • 

  • A second floating button sits next to it — a shortcut for Settings → Bars & Menus → Toolbar → "Show toolbar," so it works the same way whether you're in zen mode or not. Click it, or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + X, to show or hide the toolbar; the choice applies everywhere and is remembered next time
    • 

  • If you'd rather zen mode hide the toolbar by default, turn "Show toolbar" off before maximizing — everything it holds is still reachable by keyboard shortcut (see the other sections on this page) or by right-clicking a node for the icon row and "More" menu
    • 

  • Settings → Zen mode → "Hide app bar" also hides the very top row (Documents/Templates, search, Settings, Help, Import/Export) while zen — on by default. If Quick Assist is normally docked in the app bar ("Dock in app bar" in Settings → Quick Assist), zen mode relocates it into the status bar for as long as zen mode is on instead, rather than popping the app bar back open every time you invoke it; your "Dock in app bar" preference itself is untouched and Quick Assist returns to the app bar when you exit zen mode. If the app bar is hidden, right-click the editor canvas for a "Show app bar" option (only appears while it's actually hidden), or use the keyboard shortcuts for whatever you need — everything the app bar holds still works that way too
    • 

  • Settings → Zen mode → "Use browser fullscreen" — on by default — additionally requests the browser's own fullscreen (the same as pressing F11) when you enter zen mode, hiding the browser's tabs and address bar too, not just Sakura's own UI. Exiting fullscreen — Esc, F11, or the browser's own control — exits zen mode at the same time, so the two never end up out of sync
    • 




          


Export as PDF


    

  • Export ▾ → PDF renders the document straight from its current content and opens the browser's print dialog — choose "Save as PDF" there. No separate step needed first
    • 

  • Headings come from the Heading 1–6 style you apply in the editor (Format toolbar, next to Text color) — not from tree depth. A node with no heading style of its own renders as plain body text in the export, unless Settings → Preview → "Headings & Contents" has a level assigned to that node's depth (see below)
    • 

  • Settings → Preview → "Headings & Contents" → "Heading fallback by depth" lets you assign a heading level to depths 0–5, so an unstyled node can still render as a heading based purely on how deep it sits in the tree. An explicit heading style on the node always wins over this; depths left as "None" behave exactly as before. This only changes how exports render — it never writes a heading style into the actual document
    • 

  • A table of contents page is built from headings and [Section] markers and included at the start of every PDF export — what it includes is configurable in Settings → Preview → "Headings & Contents": cap it to a maximum heading level, or turn off section markers to keep it to real headings only. "Treat depth 0 as section markers" there (off by default) makes every top-level node act as a [Section] divider automatically, without needing the [Bracket] text — [Bracket] text still works at any depth on top of this, including depth 0. This changes the document itself: the outline canvas, exports, and rich-text copy all pick up the same section styling, not just the contents page. The contents page only appears once there are 2+ headings
    • 

  • Settings → Preview → "Export" options cover a branding mark on the cover page and every page corner (off by default, with your own text); Settings → Export & copy → "Cover page" adds a title page before the contents page
    • 

  • Notes render as their real rich content (images, lists, links) in exports, not the small dot from the editor
    • 




          


Large trees


    

  • Click ▾/▸ → fold / unfold subtree
    • 

  • ← / → → collapse / expand selected
    • 

  • Ctrl/Cmd + F → search this tree; Ctrl/Cmd + H → search and replace (Replace / Replace all, undoable)
    • 

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + C / ▶ in toolbar → collapse all (folds every top-level section)
    • 

  • Same shortcut / same button again → expand all — it's a single toggle, the icon flips to show which one it'll do next
    • 




          


Documents & folders


    

  •  button in file explorer header → new folder;  button → new document (unfiled); or Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + N from anywhere
    • 

  • Hover a folder → ＋ creates a document already filed there; ✎ renames it;  deletes it (subfolders move up a level, documents move to Unfiled — Undo appears briefly after deleting)
    • 

  • Right-click a folder → new document or new subfolder here, rename, or delete
    • 

  • Right-click a document → rename, duplicate, move to a folder, or move to Trash
    • 

  • Click ✎ / ⧉ /  icons on a document row → rename / duplicate / move to Trash; the folder-icon button moves it via a dropdown list
    • 

  • Click a document's icon (left of its name) → pick from a small set of icons to mark it visually, or "Use default icon" to clear it back to the plain page icon. Purely visual, doesn't affect the document's content
    • 

  • Click a document's or folder's name → switch to it / expand it
    • 

  • Folders can be nested: drag a folder onto another folder's top or bottom edge to reorder it as a sibling there, or onto the middle to nest it inside
    • 

  • Drag a document onto a folder (or "Unfiled") to file it there; drag it onto another document to reorder within that folder/Unfiled
    • 

  •  /  buttons by "Documents" → collapse all / expand all folders (only shown once a folder exists)
    • 

  • Ctrl/Cmd-click a document to multi-select; Shift-click selects a range. A bar appears to move or trash the whole selection at once
    •
